title: Verify Temper Windows dependency modes after product relocation
description: Temper was structurally relocated into its standalone swift-universal product repository before compatibility repair. Its original version requirement could not resolve because temper-swift had no release tag, and a one-sided local swift-argument-parser override created a duplicate package identity.
resolution: Published the already portal-pinned Temper/Windows specialization commit c38471687fd5144345851931fe0960640d42ed58 to temper-swift main, changed Temper's unreleased specialization dependency to the published main branch, and removed the invalid one-sided local ArgumentParser override. Canonical Temper now builds and its three command-composition tests pass on Windows in default remote mode; local temper-swift mode also builds without duplicate identities.

historicalContent.expectedBehavior: Temper builds and tests on Windows from its canonical product repository in both default remote-dependency mode and an explicitly selected compatible local-dependency mode.
currentEvidence: swift package dump-package succeeded from private/product-lines/temper.
SwiftPM resolved the temper-swift dependency from its existing standalone checkout.
The controlled swift-argument-parser checkout produced a duplicate package-identity warning against temper-swift's remote dependency.
GenerateDoccReference.swift failed because GeneratePlugin was unavailable and the @main type had no recognized main entry point under Swift 6.4 on Windows.
After removing the unsupported local ArgumentParser override, SPM_USE_LOCAL_DEPS=true built successfully against the portal-pinned temper-swift checkout.
After publishing temper-swift c384716 to main, default remote resolution pinned that revision and swift build completed successfully on Windows.
swift test completed successfully with three tests in the Temper command composition suite.
acceptanceCriteria: Run swift build and swift test successfully from the canonical Temper repository on Windows using the default dependency mode.
Define one compatible controlled-local dependency graph without duplicate swift-argument-parser identities.
Remove the unsupported one-sided ArgumentParser override so the compatible published plugin graph is used on Windows.
Save concise build and test evidence in the Temper product Kura space.
historicalContent.scopeBoundary: Complete the repository relocation independently; perform dependency and toolchain compatibility changes only in the canonical Temper repository.
